text: Your successor kept the easy habits. Within a generation the ministries were sponsors first and ministries second.
The schools closed one at a time. The screens never did. The country forgot how the bridges worked.
The last engineer died without an apprentice. The garbage, at least, was very well advertised.
The country carried on, as countries do. Some things got fixed, some things got worse, and the two lists were roughly the same length.
Generations passed in a comfortable, exhausting stalemate. Nobody won. Nobody had to.
Centuries on, the country is a footnote in someone else's history, and honestly not a bad one.
Your successor inherited institutions that worked, which turned out to be the whole trick.
The schools produced engineers. The engineers produced ships. The ships were dull and safe and left on schedule.
The country is remembered for being competent, which is rarer than being great and lasts longer.
